title: Who Should Make the Decisions? | Principles of Management Ep 26
description:
Who should make the decisions in a growing business? Chai Corner now has five outlets and a small head office, and every bigger decision still waits for Ravi. The college outlet wants a student offer, the bus stand needs an extra helper, and by the time Ravi answers, three days have gone. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai chain to understand centralization and decentralization, step by step.

You will learn what centralization means (the power to decide is kept at the top) and what decentralization means (that power is spread to lower levels and units, as delegation across the whole organization, done by plan). We move a slider and watch six real decisions travel between head office and the outlets, and meet Henri Fayol, who called it a simple question of proportion. Then we cover when to lean central (a small firm, uniform rules, a crisis), when to lean local (a large, spread out or fast changing firm), and how Ravi splits his decisions: menu, prices and quality stay at head office, while shifts, stock and local offers move to the outlet managers. At work today, we look at a bank setting loan rates centrally, a head nurse planning her ward roster, a product recall and city sales teams. We also look at the human side: tight control and one standard on one side, fast decisions and trusted people on the other, and the price each one pays.

This is Episode 26 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
